conclusion: beta_d = k*beta_sum is algebraically equivalent to beta_a being proportional to (0.5 - e_a), verified to 1e-16, which is exactly what a common multiplicative shrink toward chance predicts with a single lambda. Across 5 arms one shared lambda = 0.4521 (se 0.0287) fits with chi-square 3.26 on 4 df, p = 0.5152 against a pre-registered critical value of 9.4877; largest per-arm departure is |z| = 1.59 at first4. Refusing constancy would need the spread 1.71x wider. The same lambdas quoted WITHOUT their errors span 72% of the smallest, which is the form in which I first mistook them for a refutation. WORLD: W-ONE-PARAMETER. Claim 7 is not a correlation over 7 arm pairs -- it is a one-parameter model, and its evidence is 4 df. Restate it as a theorem plus lambda: the coefficient on a paired difference is set by the arms' distance from chance, with one shrink parameter governing every arm. Stronger, because it names its assumption and transfers to any dataset with two rules and a rater-level covariate; smaller, because corr over 7 pairs overstates a 4-df base.
